name: riya-game-platformer-open-world
description: riya open world · The Open Line — all twenty-eight riya worlds stitched into ONE continuous 722-unit map you run left-to-right with a follow camera: the math window recenters on riya every frame (clamped to the world edges, with a small lead toward her facing), so the whole curriculum — number line → functions → limits → calculus → series → multivar → Fourier — is one unbroken run. Merged from the riya-level-* atoms' own data (platforms, stars, curve overlays, guides, field vectors, treasure rings, gates, pads, sequences, area fills, drift regions): each world keeps its exact terrain and pedagogy as a zone; staircase bridges climb/descend between zone exit and entry heights, and entering a zone fires a name banner and swaps the skate equation. Skating is global: every skate world's curve is concatenated into one strictly-increasing mega-curve for std-platformer-body, densely resampled (monotone cubic, kinks preserved) so the ride and the drawing are the same smooth surface. GAME ELEMENTS: ✖ patrol bugs pace beats in six zones (std-patrol-hazard) and cost a life on touch; three glowing star doors (std-gate-lock) open at 20/50/80 ★; a treasure ring floats above the Gallery bars — loop one full revolution around the floating chest (std-loop-lock tracks your winding angle: θ = 2π opens it) and it spills 5 bonus 💎★; two velocity gates (std-velocity-gate) guard bonus gems off the through-path — cross the Deriv ramp gate inside its speed band (your speed IS the derivative) and hold still at the Mountain summit (slope 0) until the dwell opens it; twelve floor pads (std-pad-lock) form one world-wide checklist — mirrored pairs on the Valley and Shifts parabolas (lighting one side demands its mirror), one pad on each Corner wall, and two ordered rows on the Volume slabs where the inner sum's row must finish before the outer's (Σ); the ground itself teaches too: Doubling's floating steps double their gaps until one beats any jump (take the spring), the Series steps converge under a bonus cluster that hovers at the limit, Decay's landing pads shrink ×0.7 each, the Pole's asymptote gets a star trail up the void, and Log's domain simply has no floor left of x = −7 — jump the gap; four area fills (std-area-fill) turn motion into painted integrals — shade the Area run's region by pacing it, climb the Accum gauge fastest on the bump's high shelf, finish the Tail's finite area long before its infinite run ends, and keep the Taylor ride-band alive only while truly skating the wave; drift fields push riya like weather — cubic's inflection tugs from both sides, the vector step is a constant right-up current, gradient's arrows are the easy path uphill, the saddle's downdraft slams every jump over the pass (the max shoves you back down to the trail), and the contour patrol bobs on a sine; checkpoints at every zone entry (std-lives) are the respawn — three lives, then game over → retry. MATH YOU FEEL: while skating, std-learn-slope-probe draws the live tangent line, a rise-over-run triangle, and a glowing curve window under riya, with a dy/dx chip in the HUD; std-fx-trail leaves a comet trail. A GIF tutorial modal (std-tutorial-overlay) teaches run/jump, skating, and stars-doors on first boot. Catch every ★ the line offers — stars and spilled gems alike — to clear it. Rendered through math-canvas on theme-token grid/axes with per-family zone bands.

name: riya-game-platformer
description: riya the dot escapes the rail. In riya-game she was a bead slid ALONG the graphs; here the graphs are the landscape and she runs and jumps across them on foot. Twenty-eight worlds, one per math idea, all composed from the std game substrate — platformer-body (run/jump physics, one-way AABB terrain collision, pit-fall signal, curve-skating) + objective-flow (win gate) + fx-particles — rendered through math-canvas so the axes, the numbers, and the world's own function curve stay visible at all times. The arc: 1) The Plain — the number line as flat ground with pits; x is a number you stand on. 2) The Ramp — a staircase rising 1 per 2 across; slope is how fast you climb. 3) The Valley — y = x²/16 sampled into bars; you drop into the parabola and jump back up its walls. 4) The Mountain — a climb to the one summit star: the local maximum, where the slope flattens to zero. 5) The Pole — the ground rises toward a chasm at x = 3 that swallows you: the asymptote, the x the world never touches. 6) The Doubling Stair — steps of 1, 2, 4, 8: each costs double, and the last wall is too tall for your legs unless you find the springboard. 7) The Gallery — a Riemann skyline: the bars ARE the function, and you walk across its area. 8) Shifts — the same valley moved right 4: (x−4) transforms the function. 9) Corner — y = |x|/2: the slope jumps from −½ to +½ at a point with no slope. 10) Inflection — x³: steep, flat, steep; the slope's slope flips sign. 11) Log — ln(x+7): a burst that flattens forever, forbidden left of x = −7. 12) Derivative — the ramp you skate IS world 3's slope, drawn beside its ghost. 13) Area — the shaded region piles up behind you as you run: integration. 14) Accumulation — a hill whose height collects a dashed bump. 15) Decay — exponential decay toward a floor you never touch (y′ = −ky). 16) Tail — 1 + 12/(x+12): an infinite tail whose area stays finite (improper integral). 17) Series — steps 1, ½, ¼, … that never cross the ceiling 2 (geometric series). 18) Taylor — a line and a cubic hugging the sine wave you skate. 19) Vectors — every tread is the same displacement ⟨1.6, 1⟩; walking adds vectors tip-to-tail. 20) Contours — the skyline is a slice of the hill z = 7 − x²/16, with level lines z = 2, 4, 6 behind it. 21) Partials — the plane z = 3 + x/4 + y/2 slopes ¼ under your feet and ½ in the dashed direction. 22) Gradient — purple ∇f arrows always aim at the summit of the gaussian hill. 23) Saddle — the pass is the trail's minimum and the cross-trail's maximum at once. 24) Volume — each column is one sum; the climb across is the second sum: ∬ f dA. Every world: catch every ★ to clear; fall in a pit and riya climbs back at her spawn with every star kept — no punishment, this is a beginner's mountain Each world is its own atom under riya/atoms (riya-level-*) owning its entity contract, knobs, and page; this organism only rebinds them.

name: riya-game
description: Riya — a math journey GAME with real physics, structured as an app: a collection of orbitals, one per world, plus a menu. Riya is a dot, a point in space with MASS: the player pushes it with arrows / WASD (hold to accelerate — keyMap/keyUpMap on the math-canvas) or taps the d-pad (velocity impulses), and the std-motion-body authority integrates gravity, acceleration, speed, damping, and walls every 50ms. Seven worlds climb the math ladder: the number line (/riya-line — coast and brake onto the ★ numbers), functions (/riya-curve — riya rides y = 0.25x² − 4, the rule picks your height), the derivative (/riya-slope — the hill's slope pushes back through motion-body's bias field; park where slope = 0), the turning points (/riya-peak — a cubic's hilltop and valley, both flat spots of f(x) = 0.5x³ − 1.5x), the limit (/riya-limit — ride f(x) = 8/x toward the wall at x = 0 and watch the f(x) chip explode), the exponential (/riya-expo — the doubling curve 2^(x/2) − 1, flat then a rocket), and the integral (/riya-area — walk the strip, paint every column, watch area = … add up). Numbers are always on screen: tick labels on every axis and live HUD chips (x, v, f(x), slope, area) next to the ★ score, a velocity arrow on riya, and the tangent line under it on the slope world. EVENT HYGIENE (learned the hard way): the client runtime drains its actor queue in FIFO, so a per-tick event subscription floods it and everything lags — this game therefore keeps ticks SET-ONLY (motion integrates; the play trait's gameTick collects stars / paints strips / writes the hill bias directly onto the shared entity) and reserves events for sparse, meaningful occurrences: keydown/keyup thrust, d-pad impulses, a star collected (BURST + PROGRESS), the gate's GAME_END. Each world composes std-motion-body + std-objective-flow + std-fx-particles with events renamed per world; collection runs in the play trait's gameTick because std-objective-reach's contract is discrete HERO_STEPPED steps, not continuous motion (see Almadar_Std_Game_Gaps.md). RiyaMenuOrbital (/riya) is the shell: title plus a button per world that (navigate ...)s into it. Clearing a world pops its clear overlay; Next ▶ navigates to the next world's page — and the final world's overlay is the RIYA COMPLETE celebration, returning to the menu. CONFLICT LAYER (v5.1): every good game needs an obstacle, and in riya the obstacle is the math itself — the misconception made physical. The LIMIT world's pole is a hazard: cross the danger line at x = 0.85 and the asymptote flings riya back and takes the last collected ★ (inDanger edge-guard so one entry = one penalty). The DOUBLING world has an antagonist: a second motion-body (the ghost, labeled 2^n) steered by the gameTick toward riya with acceleration ghostThrust·2^(stars held) — every ★ you carry doubles its hunger; a catch costs the last ★ and teleports the ghost back to its spawn (ghostArmed re-arm hysteresis at rearmDistance 2 prevents chain-drains). The AREA world's final ★ is a concept gate: gray and uncollectible until all 16 strips are painted — you cannot finish before the whole sum is laid down. (Pages are mount-scoped in the playground runtime, so cross-page run state like a persistent star bank would need a persistence-backed entity — out of scope; each world's HUD tracks its own ★ score.)
